name: DB
description: DB uses the fixed-declining balance method to compute depreciation for a particular period.
tldr: Calculates declining balance depreciation for a specified period.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Value at the end of the depreciation life.

parameters.name: life
parameters.description: Number of periods over which the asset is depreciated.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The period for which to calculate depreciation.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Number of months in the first year (default 12).

basicExample.explanation: A $10,000 asset with a $2,000 salvage value and 5-year life depreciates $1,840 in the first year under declining balance.

advancedExamples.title: Partial first year
advancedExamples.description: Asset purchased in April depreciates for 9 months the first year
advancedExamples.explanation: Only 9 months of depreciation are taken in the first year.

howItWorks: DB applies a declining depreciation rate to the remaining book value of the asset. The rate is calculated as 1 - (salvage/cost)^(1/life), rounded to three decimal places.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Uses a fixed rate that does not change.
Can result in total depreciation not reaching salvage value exactly.
The first and last periods can be adjusted with the month argument.

commonErrors.cause: Period is less than 1 or greater than life, or cost < salvage.
commonErrors.fix: Check period and ensure cost is greater than or equal to salvage.

commonErrors.cause: Month argument was omitted for a partial first year.
commonErrors.fix: Include the month argument if the asset was not purchased at the start of the year.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DB works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between DB and DDB?
faq.answer: DB uses a fixed declining rate. DDB lets you specify a higher rate, usually double the straight-line rate.

faq.question: Does DB ever reach salvage value?
faq.answer: DB may not reach salvage exactly due to the fixed rate calculation.
